title: A deploy script that cleans up and never half-publishes
diff:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

release_dir="/srv/app/releases/$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
staging="$(mktemp -d)"
cleanup() { rm -rf "$staging"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

tar -xzf "$1" -C "$staging"
mkdir -p "$release_dir"
cp -a "$staging/." "$release_dir/"

ln -sfn "$release_dir" /srv/app/current.tmp
mv -T /srv/app/current.tmp /srv/app/current

concepts.description: A trap on EXIT runs the handler however the script ends, including after a failed command under set -e, so temporary files do not leak.
concepts.context: trap cleanup EXIT in deploy.sh removes the mktemp directory even when tar fails

concepts.description: Creating a symlink under a temporary name and renaming it over the live one is a single atomic step, so readers see the old release or the new one, never neither.
concepts.context: deploy.sh builds current.tmp and mv -T it over /srv/app/current instead of removing and recreating the link

concepts.description: An unquoted variable is split on whitespace and globbed, so a path with a space becomes several arguments.
concepts.context: "$staging" and "$release_dir" are quoted in every command of deploy.sh

concepts.description: Unpacking into a fresh private directory first means a failed extraction never touches the live release tree.
concepts.context: deploy.sh extracts the archive into mktemp -d before copying into the release directory
